beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That gives readers a practical way to challenge negative answers from automated research systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A complete trace can still lead faithfully from a false source to a false conclusion.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Provenance explains origin, while credibility and authority require additional evidence and policies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A quotation, a statistical estimate, and a formal proof carry different statuses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed system must preserve those distinctions across its computational steps.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It must also distinguish generated candidates from claims admitted for a particular purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No single confidence score can replace all those relationships.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book’s trust argument becomes interesting precisely where traceability stops being sufficient.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three prototypes approach different parts of this architectural question.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One emphasizes persistent knowledge and the bounded selection of circuits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Another examines coding agents as compilers of documents into candidate procedures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A third emphasizes supported language, reviewable witnesses, abstention, and authority gates.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their differences remain visible rather than being presented as one finished implementation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They demonstrate mechanisms without establishing broad language coverage or general superiority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The prototype chapter gives readers something concrete against which to test the larger research vision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Scientific peer review illustrates the mixture of exact checks and legitimate interpretation.
